paper_metadata.title: Diffusion Tensor Imaging Reveals Elevated Diffusivity of White Matter Microstructure that Is Independently Associated with Long-Term Outcome after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A TRACK-TBI Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, multi-center prospective cohort (TRACK-TBI) with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and a demographically matched control group. While there is some attrition from the total enrolled sample to the MRI sub-sample, the authors demonstrate that the sub-sample is representative of the larger cohort.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: From Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury (TRACK-TBI), a cohort study at 11 United States level 1 trauma centers, a total of 391 patients with acute mTBI ages 17 to 60 years were included
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as patients presenting to Level 1 trauma centers with mTBI.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were enrolled at 11 academic level 1 trauma centers in the United States within 24 h of injury, after evaluation in the Emergency Department (ED) or hospital inpatient unit for TBI
items.reasoning: Recruitment methods and the sampling frame (ED/Inpatient) are explicitly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: While the follow-up intervals are described, the specific calendar years of recruitment for this specific analysis are not explicitly stated in the main text.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location) are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 11 academic level 1 trauma centers in the United States
items.reasoning: The setting and geographic scope are clearly defined.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: mTBI participants met inclusion criteria of admission GCS 13–15, had clinical head CT scans, and were enrolled within 24 h of injury... Children age <17 years and adults >60 years were excluded
items.reasoning: Criteria include GCS scores, age limits, and timing from injury.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of 484 participants with mTBI in the target age range, 93 were excluded for incomplete DTI scans at one or both time points
items.reasoning: While the sample is large, a significant portion of the eligible MRI-scanned cohort was excluded due to image quality/motion, though the authors argue the final sample remains representative.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: There were no significant group differences in age (mTBI: 34.6±12.5 years; FC: 33.6±11.4 years; p=0.35), sex (mTBI: 132 women, 259 men; FC: 48 women, 100 men; p=0.77), or years of education
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical characteristics (GCS, CT findings) are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is significant attrition from the initial enrollment (1132) to the final analyzed sample (391), largely due to the requirements for research MRI at two time points and image quality. However, the authors performed a sensitivity check showing the analyzed sample matches the broader cohort's outcome distribution.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of these mTBI participants, 592 underwent MRI at both two weeks... 391 patients were available for analysis, of whom 367 had GOSE scores recorded at six-month follow-up.
items.reasoning: The drop from 592 eligible for MRI to 367 with complete data and outcomes represents a roughly 38% loss of the MRI-eligible sub-group.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not detail specific efforts to re-engage or collect data on those who missed the 6-month scan or outcome interview.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 93 were excluded for incomplete DTI scans at one or both time points—e.g., excessive motion during scan and/or visible image artifacts.
items.reasoning: Technical reasons for exclusion from the analysis are provided.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The characteristics of the imaged patients with mTBI are comparable to that of the entire enrolled sample, as previously published in Nelson and coworkers
items.reasoning: The authors refer to a previous publication to justify representativeness but do not provide a direct table comparing those lost vs. those retained in this specific paper.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: 53% of the imaged patients and 53% of the entire cohort manifesting GOSE <8 at long-term outcome. Therefore, there does not appear to be a major selection bias
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly compare the outcome rates between the analyzed sample and the total cohort to rule out informative censoring.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (DTI metrics) were measured using a highly standardized multi-center protocol with rigorous quality control, including phantoms and traveling volunteers to ensure cross-site reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Axial diffusivity (AD), fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were the measures of WM microstructure.
items.reasoning: The DTI metrics are standard and clearly identified.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Standardization of DTI measures across all 13 MR scanners at the 11 sites was achieved using both an isotropic diffusion phantom developed at the NIST and a traveling volunteer
items.reasoning: The use of NIST phantoms and traveling volunteers is the gold standard for multi-center DTI reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Standardized score for each DTI measure was calculated using its mean and standard deviation from the analysis sample.
items.reasoning: DTI metrics were treated as continuous variables (standardized scores) in the regression models.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Whole-brain DTI acquisition was performed with a multi-slice single-shot spin echo echoplanar pulse sequence using 64 diffusion-encoding directions... b=1300 s/mm²
items.reasoning: A standardized pulse sequence was used across all 11 sites.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 391 patients were available for analysis
items.reasoning: The analysis was restricted to those with complete, high-quality DTI data.

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study appears to use complete-case analysis for the DTI metrics rather than imputation.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOSE) is a validated, standard measure in TBI research. The assessment was performed at a fixed time point (6 months) and specifically focused on injury-related disability.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The primary outcome was the Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) score of injury-related functional limitations across broad life domains at six months post-injury.
items.reasoning: The outcome and its timing are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The GOSE was administered to capture disability related to the TBI only, with exclusion of disability associated with co-occurring polytrauma
items.reasoning: The GOSE is a validated tool, and the study used central curation to ensure data quality.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The six-month follow-up GOSE was administered... (range: 160–203 days).
items.reasoning: The outcome was measured consistently for all participants within a specified window.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, utilizing voxelwise analysis followed by ROI-based regression. The authors adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg method and checked for multicollinearity.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy

items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline is described in detail.

items.evidence_snippet: adjusting for demographic and other known risk factors such as history of psychiatric illness, previous TBI, and CT imaging results
items.reasoning: Variables were selected based on known risk factors in TBI literature.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: logistic regression models... Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method was used to adjust for multiple testing.
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the dichotomized GOSE outcome, and BH adjustment controls the false discovery rate.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Global FA, MD, and RD at two weeks did not show significant bivariate associations with six-month GOSE.
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings for all four DTI metrics.
